items.fromString:
h3. Description of problem:

When running oc oadp backup-location set <BSL_NAME> --cacert <path> on a BSL that is managed by a DPA, the CLI accepts the input and returns "configured successfully". However, the DPA reconciler immediately overwrites the change back to the value defined in the DPA spec. 
The CLI should error out, informing the user to modify the DPA instead.

Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

How reproducible:

Steps to Reproduce:

# Create a DPA with invalid caCert. The managed BSL becomes Unavailable.
{noformat}apiVersion: oadp.openshift.io/v1alpha1
kind: DataProtectionApplication
metadata:
  name: ts-dpa
  namespace: openshift-adp
spec:
  backupLocations:
  - velero:
      config:
        insecureSkipTLSVerify: "false"
        profile: noobaa
        region: noobaa
        s3ForcePathStyle: "true"
        s3Url: https://s3-openshift-storage.apps.oadp-abcd123.qe.devcluster.openshift.com
      credential:
        key: cloud
        name: cloud-credentials
      default: true
      objectStorage:
        bucket: oadpabcd1234
        prefix: velero-cacert-test
        caCert: $GARBAGE_CERT (invalid cacert)
      provider: aws
  configuration:
    nodeAgent:
      enable: true
      uploaderType: kopia
    velero:
      defaultPlugins:
      - openshift
      - aws{noformat}
# Attempt to fix the BSL using the OADP CLI with valid cacert :
{noformat}$ oc oadp backup-location set ts-dpa-1 --cacert /tmp/cluster-ca.crt -n openshift-adp

Backup storage location "ts-dpa-1" configured successfully.{noformat}
# Check BSL status :
{noformat}$ oc get bsl ts-dpa-1 -n openshift-adp
NAME       PHASE         LAST VALIDATED   AGE   DEFAULT
ts-dpa-1   Unavailable   13s              78m   true{noformat}

     BSL remains Unavailabl, the DPA reconciler reverted the valid cert back to the DPA's invalid cert.

 4. The same behavior occurs in reverse: with a valid cacert DPA, patching the BSL with an invalid --cacert is also silently reverted and the BSL remains Available.

h4. Actual results:

The CLI returns "configured successfully" on a DPA-managed BSL. The change is silently reverted by the DPA reconciler. 

Expected results:

The CLI should error when the user tries to modify a DPA managed BSL with --cacert flag via OADP CLI.
(may be something like -
Error: BackupStorageLocation "ts-dpa-1" is managed by DPA "ts-dpa". Modify the DataProtectionApplication resource instead.)

Additional info:

Found while drafting a polarian test case - [https://polarion.engineering.redhat.com/polarion/#/project/OADP/workitem?id=OADP-825|https://polarion.engineering.redhat.com/polarion/#/project/OADP/workitem?id=OADP-825]

When running oc oadp backup-location set on a DPA-managed BSL, the CLI returns "configured successfully" but the DPA reconciler immediately overwrites the changes for --cacert and --credential flags. The --default flag is the only one that persists.
The CLI should error out when the user tries to modify a DPA-managed BSL, informing the user to modify the DPA instead.

Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

How reproducible:

Steps to Reproduce:

# Create a DPA with invalid caCert. The managed BSL becomes Unavailable.
{noformat}apiVersion: oadp.openshift.io/v1alpha1
kind: DataProtectionApplication
metadata:
  name: ts-dpa
  namespace: openshift-adp
spec:
  backupLocations:
  - velero:
      config:
        insecureSkipTLSVerify: "false"
        profile: noobaa
        region: noobaa
        s3ForcePathStyle: "true"
        s3Url: https://s3-openshift-storage.apps.oadp-abcd123.qe.devcluster.openshift.com
      credential:
        key: cloud
        name: cloud-credentials
      default: true
      objectStorage:
        bucket: oadpabcd1234
        prefix: velero-cacert-test
        caCert: $GARBAGE_CERT (invalid cacert)
      provider: aws
  configuration:
    nodeAgent:
      enable: true
      uploaderType: kopia
    velero:
      defaultPlugins:
      - openshift
      - aws{noformat}
# Attempt to fix the BSL using the OADP CLI with valid cacert (remains unavailable) :
{noformat}$ oc oadp backup-location set ts-dpa-1 --cacert /tmp/cluster-ca.crt -n openshift-adp
Backup storage location "ts-dpa-1" configured successfully.

$ oc get bsl ts-dpa-1 -n openshift-adp
NAME       PHASE         LAST VALIDATED   AGE     DEFAULT
ts-dpa-1   Unavailable   14s              2m50s   true{noformat}
# Attempt to fix the BSL using the OADP CLI with valid credentials (remains unavailable) :
{noformat}$ oc oadp backup-location set ts-dpa-1 --cacert /tmp/cluster-ca.crt -n openshift-adp
Backup storage location "ts-dpa-1" configured successfully.

$ oc get bsl ts-dpa-1 -n openshift-adp
NAME       PHASE         LAST VALIDATED   AGE     DEFAULT
ts-dpa-1   Unavailable   14s              2m50s   true{noformat}
# Attempt to unset BSL to --default=false using the OADP CLI (changes persist)  :
{noformat}$ oc oadp backup-location set ts-dpa-1 --default=false -n openshift-adp
Backup storage location "ts-dpa-1" configured successfully.

$ oc get bsl ts-dpa-1 -n openshift-adp
NAME       PHASE         LAST VALIDATED   AGE     DEFAULT
ts-dpa-1   Unavailable   43s              3h27m  {noformat}
# The same behavior occurs in reverse: with a valid caCert DPA (BSL Available), setting --cacert /tmp/garbage-ca.crt is silently reverted and BSL remains Available.

h4. Actual results:

The CLI returns "configured successfully" on a DPA-managed BSL. The change is silently reverted by the DPA reconciler. 

Expected results:

The CLI should error when the user tries to modify a DPA managed BSL with oc oadp backup-location set via OADP CLI for --cacert & --credentials flag
(may be something like -
Error: BackupStorageLocation "ts-dpa-1" is managed by DPA "ts-dpa". Modify the DataProtectionApplication resource instead.)

Additional info:

Found while drafting a polarian test case - [https://polarion.engineering.redhat.com/polarion/#/project/OADP/workitem?id=OADP-825|https://polarion.engineering.redhat.com/polarion/#/project/OADP/workitem?id=OADP-825]

items.toString:
h3. Objective

The objective of this issue is to establish and execute an alternate PSI exit strategy for the Migration QE and MTA-QE tenants to ensure a smooth transition from OpenStack RDU2 to a new environment.

h3. Context

As part of the OpenStack Exit Flight Plan, the Migration QE team needs to migrate two tenants (Migration QE and MTA-QE) currently hosted on RHOS-01 and RHOS-D. The team has a major release scheduled for August–September, which necessitates a phased migration approach or a temporary overlap of environments to avoid service disruption.

h3. Scope

* *In-Scope:*
** Migration of the "Migration QE" tenant (AppCode: MIG-001) and "MTA-QE" tenant (AppCode: MIG-002).
** Renaming tenants in the new OpenShift environment to OADP-QE and MTA-QE.
** Provisioning a small quota in the new environment for Proof of Concept (POC) and automation updates.
** Support for RHEL-based OS images and high IOPS storage requirements.
* *Out-of-Scope:*
** Migration of projects not associated with the specified AppCodes.
** Full-scale migration prior to the completion of the August–September release unless the POC is successful.

h3. Success criteria

* Successful provisioning of a POC environment in the destination site (e.g., ITUP.Stable - IAD2 or ITUP.Scale).
* Validation of automation scripts within the new environment.
* Completion of the full migration of both tenants (OADP-QE and MTA-QE) post-September release.
* Retention of necessary data and functionality for RHEL-based workloads.

h3. Risks and dependencies

* *Release Conflict:* A major release is planned for August–September; any migration activity must not jeopardize this timeline.
* *Storage Requirements:* The project requires high IOPS storage, which must be available in the destination environment.
* *Quota Availability:* Dependency on the infrastructure team to provide a small quota for POC work before the final migration.

h3. Other information

* *Original Issue Link:* [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tEoVKpjm8BA7SrgXRQomdmbzh8P5OO-lGg7i9c1qAqs/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.h02eh3kdweab|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tEoVKpjm8BA7SrgXRQomdmbzh8P5OO-lGg7i9c1qAqs/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.h02eh3kdweab]
